text:
Proclamation of the Irish Republic, issued by Robert Emmet, July 23rd, 1803, at the outset of the second United Irishmen revolt.

You are now called on to shew to the world that you are competent to take your place among nations, that you have a right to claim their recognizance of you, as an independent country, by the only satisfactory proof you can furnish of your capability of maintaining your independence, your wresting it from England with your own hands.

In the development of this system, which has been organized within the last eight months, at the close of internal defeat and without the hope of foreign assistance; which has been conducted with a tranquillity, mistaken for obedience; which neither the failure of a similar attempt in England has retarded, nor the renewal of hostilities has accelerated; in the development of this system you will show to the people of England, that there is a spirit of perseverance in this country, beyond their power to calculate or to repress; you will show to them that as long as they think to hold unjust dominion over Ireland, under no change of circumstances can they count on its obedience; under no aspect of affairs can they judge of its intentions; you will show to them that the question which it now behoves them to take into serious and instant consideration, is not, whether they will resist a separation, which it is our fixed determination to effect, but whether or not, they will drive us beyond separation; whether they will by a sanguinary resistance create a deadly national antipathy between the two countries, or whether they will take the only means still left, of driving such a sentiment from our minds, a prompt, manly, and sagacious acquiescence, in our just and unalterable determination.

If the secrecy with which the present effort has been conducted, shall have led our enemies to suppose that its extent must have been partial, a few days will undeceive them. That confidence, which was once lost, by trusting to external support, and suffering our own means to be gradually undermined, has been again restored. We have been mutually pledged to each other, to look only to our own strength, and that the first introduction of a system of terror, the first attempt to execute an individual in one county, should be the signal of insurrection in all. We have now, without the loss of a man, with our means of communication untouched, brought our plans to the moment when they are ripe for execution, and in the promptitude with which nineteen counties will come forward at once to execute them, it will be found that neither confidence nor communication are wanting to the people of Ireland.

In calling on our countrymen to come forward, we feel ourselves bound, at the same time, to justify our claim to their confidence by a precise declaration of our views. We therefore solemnly declare, that our object is to establish a free and independent republic in Ireland: that the pursuit of this object we will relinquish only with our lives: that we will never, unless at the express call of our country, abandon our post, until the acknowledgment of its independence is obtained from England; and that we will enter into no negotiation (but for exchange of prisoners) with the government of that country while a British army remains in Ireland. Such is the declaration which we call on the people of Ireland to support — And we call first on that part of Ireland which was once paralysed by the want of intelligence, to shew that to that cause only was its inaction to be attributed; on that part of Ireland which was once foremost, by its fortitude in suffering; on that part of Ireland which once offered to take the salvation of the country on itself; on that part of Ireland where the flame of liberty first glowed; we call upon the NORTH to stand up and shake off their Slumber and their oppression.

MEN of LEINSTER, stand to your arms.

To the courage which you have already displayed, is your country indebted for the confidence which it now feels in its own strength, and for the dismay with which our enemies will be overwhelmed when they shall find this effort to be universal. But men of Leinster, you owe more to your country than the having animated it by your past example; you owe more to your own courage, than the having obtained, by it a protection. If six years ago, when you rose without arms, without plan, without co-operation, with more troops against you alone, than are now in the country at large; you were able to remain for six weeks in open defiance of the government, and within a few miles of the capital what will you not now effect, with that capital, and every other part of Ireland ready to support you? But it is not on this head that we have need to address you. No we now speak to you, and through you, to the rest of Ireland, on a subject, dear to us even as the success of our country, — its honour. You are accused by your enemies of having violated that honour; excesses which they themselves had in their fullest extent provoked, but which they have grossly exaggerated, have been attributed to you. The opportunity of vindicating yourselves by actions, is now for the first time before you; and we call upon you to give the lie to such assertions, by carefully avoiding every appearance of plunder, intoxication, or revenge; recollecting that you lost Ireland before, not from want of courage, but from not having that courage rightly directed by discipline. But we trust that your past sufferings, have taught you experience, and that you will respect the declaration which we now make and which we are determined by every means in our power to enforce.

The nation alone possesses the right of punishing individuals, and whosoever shall put another person to death, except in battle, without a fair trial by his country, is guilty of murder. The intention of the provisional government of Ireland, is to claim from the English government, such Irishmen as have been sold or transported, by it for their attachment to freedom; and for this purpose, it will retain as hostages for their safe return, such adherents of that government as shall fall into its hands. It therefore calls upon the people to respect those hostages, and to recollect that in spilling their blood, they would leave their own countrymen in the hands of their enemies.

The intention of the provisional government, is to resign its functions, as soon as the nation shall have chosen its delegates, but in the mean time, it is determined to enforce the regulations hereunto subjoined; — It in consequence takes the property of the country under its protection, and will punish with the utmost rigour any person who shall violate that property, and thereby injure the present resources and the future prosperity of Ireland.

Whoever refuses to march to whatever part of the country he is ordered, is guilty of disobedience to the government, which alone is competent to decide in what place his services are necessary, and which desires him to recollect, that in whatever part of Ireland he is fighting, he is still fighting for its freedom.

Whoever presumes by acts or otherwise to give countenance to the calumny propagated by our enemies, that this is a religious contest, is guilty of the grievous crime of belying the motives of his country. Religious disqualification is but one of the many grievances of which Ireland has to complain. Our intention is to remove not that only, but every other oppression under which we labour. We fight, that all of us may have our country, and that done — each of us shall have his religion.

We are aware of the apprehensions which you have expressed, that in quitting your own counties, you leave your wives and children, in the hands of your enemies; but on this head have no uneasiness. If there are still men base enough to persecute those, who are unable to resist, shew them by your victories that we have the power to punish, and by your obedience, that we have the power to protect, and we pledge ourselves to you, that these men shall be made to feel, that the safety of every thing they hold dear, depends on the conduct they observe to you. Go forth then with confidence, conquer the foreign enemies of your country, and leave to us the care of preserving its internal tranquillity; recollect that not only the victory, but also the honour of your country, is placed in your hands; give up your private resentments, and shew to the world, that the Irish, are not only a brave, but also a generous and forgiving people.

MEN of MUNSTER and CONNAUGHT

You have your instructions, we trust that you will execute them. The example of the rest of your countrymen is now before you; your own strength is unbroken;-five months ago you were eager to act without any other assistance. We now call upon you to shew, what you then declared you only wanted the opportunity of proving, that you possess the same love of liberty and the same courage with which the rest of your countrymen are animated.

We now turn to that portion of our countrymen whose prejudices we had rather overcome by a frank declaration of our intentions, than conquer their persons in the field; and in making this declaration, we do not wish to dwell on events, which, however, they may bring tenfold odium on their authors, must still tend to keep alive in the minds both of the instruments and victims of them, a spirit of animosity which it is our wish to destroy. We will therefore enter into no detail of the atrocities and oppression which Ireland has laboured under during its connexion with England; but we justify our determination to separate from that country on the broad historical statement, that during six hundred years she has been unable to conciliate the affections of the people of Ireland; that during that time, five rebellions were entered into, to shake off the yoke; that she has been obliged to resort to a system of unprecedented torture in her defence; that she has broken every tie of voluntary connexion by taking even the name of independence from Ireland, through the intervention of a parliament notoriously bribed, and not representing the will of the people; that in her vindication of this measure she has herself given the justification of the views of the United Irishmen, by declaring in the words of her ministers,

"That Ireland never had, and never could enjoy under the then circumstances the benefit of British connexion; that it necessarily must happen when one country is connected with another, that the interests of the lesser will be borne down by those of the greater. That England has supported and encouraged the English colonists in their oppression towards the natives of Ireland; that Ireland had been left in a state of ignorance, rudeness and barbarism, worse in its effects, and more degrading in its nature, than that in which it was found six centuries before."

Now to what cause are these things to be attributed? Did the cause of the almighty keep alive a spirit of obstinacy in the minds of the Irish people for six hundred years?

Did the doctrines of the French revolution produce five rebellions? Could the misrepresentations of ambitious and designing men drive from the mind of a whole people, the recollection of defeat, and raise the infant from the cradle, with the same feelings with which his father sunk into the grave? Will this gross avowal which our enemies have made of their own views, remove none of the calumny that has been thrown upon ours? Will none of the credit [which] has been lavished on them, be transferred to the solemn declaration which we now make in the face of god and our country. We war not against property — We war against no religious sect — We war not against past opinions or prejudices — We war against English dominion. We will not however deny, that there are some men, who, not because they have supported the government of our oppressors, but because they have violated the common laws of morality, which exist alike under all or under no government; have put it beyond our power to give to them the protection of a government. We will not hazard the influence we may have with the people, and the power it may give us of preventing the excesses of revolution, by undertaking to place in tranquillity the man who has been guilty of torture, free quarters, rape and murder, by the side of the sufferer or their relations; but in the frankness with which we warn these men of their danger, let those who do not feel that they have passed this boundary of mediation, count on their safety.

We had hoped for the sake of our enemies to have taken them by surprize, and to have committed the cause of our country before they could have time to commit themselves against it, but though we have not altogether been able to succeed, we are yet rejoiced to find that they have not come forward with promptitude on the side of those who have deceived them, and we now call on them before it is yet too late, not to commit themselves further against a people they are unable to resist, and in support of a government, which, by their own declaration has forfeited its claim to their allegiance.

To that government in whose hands, though not the issue, at least the features with which the present contest is to be marked, and placed, we now turn. How is it to be decided? Is open and honourable force alone to be resorted to, or is it your intention to employ those laws which custom has placed in your hands, and to force us to employ the law of retaliation in our defence?

Of the inefficacy of a system of terror, in preventing the people of Ireland from coming forward to assert their freedom, you have already had experience. Of the effect which such a system will have on our minds in case of success, we have already forewarned you — We now address to you another consideration — If in the question which is now to receive a solemn and we trust final decision, if we have been deceived reflection would point out that conduct should be resorted to, which was the best calculated to produce conviction on our minds. What would that conduct be? It would be to shew to us that the difference of strength between the two countries [is such], as to render it unnecessary for you to bring out all your force; to shew to us that you have something in reserve wherewith to crush hereafter, not only a greater exertion on the part of the people, but a greater exertion, rendered still greater by foreign assistance: It would be to shew to us that what we have vainly supported to be a prosperity growing beyond your grasp, is only a partial exuberance requiring but the pressure of your hand to reduce it into form. But for your own sake do not resort to a system, which while it increased the acrimony of our minds would leave us under the melancholy delusion that we had been forced to yield, not to the sound and temperate exertions of superior strength, but to the frantick struggles of weakness, concealing itself under desperation. Consider also that the distinction of rebel and enemy is of a very fluctuating nature; that during the course of your own experience you have already been obliged to lay it aside; that should you be forced to abandon it towards Ireland you cannot hope to do so as tranquilly as you have done towards America, for in the exasperated state to which you have raised the minds of the Irish people; a people whom you profess to have left in a state of barbarism and ignorance, with what confidence can you say to that people "while the advantage of cruelty lay upon our side, we slaughtered you without mercy, but the measure of our own blood is beginning to preponderate, it is no longer our interest that this bloody system should continue, shew us then, that forbearance which we never taught you by precept or example, lay aside your resentments, give quarter to us, and let us mutually forget, that we never gave quarter to you." Cease then we entreat you uselessly to violate humanity by resorting to a system inefficacious as an instrument of terror, inefficacious as a mode of defence, inefficacious as a mode of conviction, ruinous to the future relations of the two countries in case of our success, and destructive of those instruments of defence which you will then find it doubly necessary to have preserved unimpaired. But if your determination be otherwise, hear ours. We will not imitate you in cruelty; we will put no man to death in cold blood, the prisoners which first fall into our hands shall be treated with the respect due to the unfortunate; but if the life of a single Irish solder is taken after the battle is over, the orders thence forth to be issued to the Irish army are neither to give or take quarter. Countrymen if a cruel necessity forces us to retaliate, we will bury our resentments in the field of battle, if we are to fall, we will fall where we fight for our country — Fully impressed with this determination, of the necessity of adhering to which past experience has but too fatally convinced us; fully impressed with the justice of our cause which we now put to issue. We make our last and solemn appeal to the sword and to Heaven; and as the cause of Ireland deserves to prosper, may God give it Victory.

- Robert Emmet.

text:
Tuesday morning headlines from #Azerbaijan, 27 October

● Azerbaijan and Iran have exchanged fresh accusations amid public anger in parts of Azerbaijani society over new secular school-uniform rules that effectively ban the wearing of hijabs in schools. Iran has offered to admit Azerbaijani girls to its universities. Azerbaijan’s Ministry of Science and Education called the remarks inappropriate and an attempt to interfere in the country’s education policy. The ministry also pointed out that Iran has no schools or universities where teaching is conducted in Azerbaijani, despite an estimated 40 million ethnic Azerbaijanis living in Iran. “For decades, they have been deprived of the opportunity to receive education in their mother tongue,” the ministry said.

● Representatives of 55 Azerbaijani NGOs have sent an open letter to Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, urging him to ensure that millions of ethnic Azerbaijanis in Iran can receive education in their mother tongue. They called for Azerbaijani to be taught in schools, for secondary schools and universities offering instruction in the language to be established, and for teachers, textbooks and curricula to be developed. The signatories described this as a matter of historical justice and offered to support educational, scientific and cultural cooperation. The letter also referred to Pezeshkian’s commitment to the Azerbaijani language and his visits to Karabakh during trips to Azerbaijan.

● Muhammed Emin Yıldırım, a representative of Turkish magazine Köklü Değişim who was previously barred from entering Azerbaijan, has been detained in Istanbul. He is among 31 Turkish citizens whom Baku accused of publishing material targeting Azerbaijan’s sovereignty and national security and inciting religious hostility. The publications supported public anger over the new secular school-uniform rules, which effectively ban hijabs in schools. The reasons for Yıldırım’s detention in Turkey and details of the investigation have not yet been disclosed.

● Oktay Saral, an adviser to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, has stepped down after publicly criticising restrictions on wearing hijabs in Azerbaijani schools. His comments prompted sharp reactions in Baku and contributed to tensions between the two countries, Azerbaijan’s service of Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported. According to the outlet, Saral resigned at Baku’s request in an effort to ease tensions, but this claim has not been independently confirmed.

● The need to address what he described as pro-Armenian disinformation published by Vatican News was raised by Allahshukur Pashazadeh, chairman of the Caucasus Muslims Board, during a meeting at the Vatican with Cardinal George Jacob Koovakad. Pashazadeh said the outlet had recently published false or one-sided reports based exclusively on Armenian sources. Koovakad said he would immediately inform the relevant Holy See bodies. The specific reports in question and any measures to be taken have not been disclosed.

● The Caucasus Muslims Board and the Holy See signed a memorandum of understanding on interfaith dialogue during the same meeting. It is the Vatican’s first such memorandum with the board; similar documents had previously been concluded mainly with state institutions. A permanent joint committee is planned to implement the agreement. The meeting also addressed cooperation between the two institutions, construction of a Catholic church in Baku — due to be completed in 2027 — and the opening of a Vatican apostolic nunciature in Azerbaijan.

● Eleven people have been arrested in Baku in connection with a fatal stabbing at a restaurant, with investigators linking them to an alleged criminal group. The incident took place on the night of 23 October, when 43-year-old local resident J. Miragaev died from stab wounds. According to Azerbaijan’s Interior Ministry, seven of the 11 detainees had previous convictions. text:
[Kannappa Nayanar](https://t.co/RifiurHr0z) was a tribal hunter who became one of the 63 revered Saiva Nayanar saints of South India, celebrated for his pure, unconditional love and self-sacrifice for Lord Shiva. His story is deeply connected to the [Sri Kalahasti Temple](https://t.co/2Bt3srYWXF) in Andhra Pradesh. [1, 2] 
## Early Life and Devotion

* Thinnan: Born as Thinnan (or Dinna) in the forest region of Uduppur/Potthapi, he was a skilled archer and the son of a tribal chief named Nagan. [2, 3, 4] 
* The Hidden Linga: While hunting in the forest, Thinnan discovered a forgotten Shiva Lingam in the Srikalahasti hills. [4, 5] 
* Unconventional Worship: Unaware of formal Vedic rituals, he worshipped the stone in his own tribal way:
* He carried water in his mouth to consecrate the Lingam.
   * He adorned it with wild forest flowers tucked into his hair.
   * He offered the best, tender portions of roasted or cooked meat from his daily hunt. [3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9] 
* The Priest's Distress: A traditional Brahmin priest named Sivagochariar was upset to find these "impure" offerings and cleaned the shrine daily, unaware of who was leaving them. Shiva eventually revealed to the priest the unmatched, genuine bhakti (devotion) of the hunter. [3, 7] 

## The Ultimate Test of Faith

* The Bleeding Eye: To test Thinnan's devotion, Lord Shiva caused one of the eyes of the Lingam to well up with blood and tears. [3, 7] 
* Plucking the First Eye: Distressed at seeing his Lord in pain, Thinnan tried medicinal leaves first. When that failed, he used his sharp arrow or knife to gouge out his own right eye and placed it on the Lingam's bleeding eye. The bleeding stopped immediately. [3, 7] 
* The Second Eye: Moments later, the second eye of the Lingam began to bleed. [3, 7] 
* The Foot Marker: Thinnan resolved to pluck out his remaining eye as well, realizing he would become blind and might miss the exact spot. To solve this, he placed his big toe directly over the bleeding eye of the stone as a marker. [3, 10] 
* Shiva's Manifestation: Just as he raised the weapon to remove his second eye, Lord Shiva's hand emerged from the Lingam to stop him. [5, 7] 

## Liberation and Legacy

* Restoration and Title: Shiva restored Thinnan's lost eye, blessed him, and gave him the name Kannappa (derived from kann, meaning eye, and appa, father/one who gave his eyes).
* Moksha: Kannappa was granted liberation (moksha) and elevated as one of the preeminent Nayanars. [3, 7]

text:
There are no U.S. rules that require media to report on or provide equal news coverage of all candidates for political office. News organizations (print, broadcast, digital, etc.) retain broad First Amendment editorial discretion to decide what is newsworthy.​
Congress
Broadcast-specific rules (FCC / Communications Act)
These apply mainly to over-the-air radio and television stations (and limited cable origination). They do not mandate proactive equal reporting or coverage of every candidate in news programming:
Equal opportunities rule (47 U.S.C. § 315, often called the “equal time” rule): If a station permits one legally qualified candidate to “use” its facilities (identifiable voice or image, outside exemptions), it must offer comparable opportunities (time and placement) to other legally qualified candidates for the same office. This covers paid ads and non-exempt free appearances.
Key exemptions (so routine news does not trigger it): bona fide newscasts, bona fide news interviews, certain news documentaries (where the candidate’s appearance is incidental), and on-the-spot coverage of bona fide news events (including many debates and conventions). Stations are not required to put any candidate on the air; the duty arises only after a non-exempt use by one candidate.​
law.cornell
Reasonable access (47 U.S.C. § 312(a)(7)): Commercial broadcasters must provide reasonable access (or allow purchase of reasonable amounts of time) to legally qualified candidates for federal office. Public stations are generally exempt from this affirmative duty.​
Jdsupra
Related rate rules (lowest unit charge in certain pre-election periods) and political file disclosure requirements also apply, but none force equal news reporting.
Fairness Doctrine
The old FCC Fairness Doctrine (1949–1987) required coverage of controversial issues of public importance and contrasting viewpoints. It was abolished and is no longer in force. It was issue-focused rather than a candidate-equal-coverage mandate.​
Wikipedia
Print, cable networks, and digital media
Miami Herald Publishing Co. v. Tornillo (1974) struck down a Florida “right of reply” statute that would have forced newspapers to give candidates equal space to respond to criticism. The Supreme Court held that compelling such publication violates the First Amendment’s protection of editorial control. Similar compelled-access rules do not apply to print or most non-broadcast media. Cable networks, streaming, social media, and websites are generally outside the equal-opportunities rules that govern licensed broadcasters.​
Wikipedia
Practical notes
“Legally qualified candidate” has a specific definition (public announcement, legal eligibility, and ballot qualification or substantial write-in showing).
Debate sponsors (e.g., Commission on Presidential Debates) set their own inclusion criteria; qualifying debates often fall under news-event exemptions.
Some other countries impose equal-access or balance rules on public broadcasters during campaigns, but that is not the U.S. system.
In short, U.S. law regulates certain access and advertising opportunities on broadcast stations once one candidate appears, but it does not require media to report on every candidate or give them equal news coverage. Editorial judgment about newsworthiness remains protected.

Dante Moore is OUT for the season - a season in which he was supposed to remain one of the Top Picks of the 2027 NFL Draft. While this is bad news for Moore, it isn't the first time he'll be carrying a quiet weight on his shoulders.

From dealing with his parents' divorce, his mother's breast cancer diagnosis, and depression, Moore has had his fair share of battles to fight. And he had to fight these battles as a freshman when he was at UCLA. These are the battles that rebuilt him.

Moore was born in East Cleveland, Ohio, and raised primarily in Detroit by his father, Otha, after his parents divorced. Otha, a Ford plant engineer who also took side jobs (landscaping, bartending at Tigers and Lions games) and coached youth teams, raised Dante and his two older siblings largely as a single parent. The family wasn’t wealthy, and that reality shaped Dante early.

As a seventh-grader, he attended a Michigan camp and received a scholarship offer from Jim Harbaugh. He didn’t fully grasp what it meant until his dad explained on the car ride home that it could cover college and ease the family’s burden.

Dante cried in the backseat. (He was already training with former Michigan QB Devin Gardner, who mentored him with early-morning workouts in Detroit.)

As an 18-year-old true freshman starter at UCLA, the pressure of high expectations hit hard. Around the same time, his mother, Jera Bohlen-Moore (a former all-state high school basketball player in Ohio), was diagnosed with breast cancer.

She usually texted via voice messages; one day he got a long typed paragraph followed by a message that said she had cancer. He dropped the phone and cried. UCLA coach Chip Kelly arranged a medical flight so Dante could go home and surprise her.

Moore later wrote in a letter that he found himself struggling deeply and that he was depressed. The combination of QB pressure at 18 and watching his mom go through chemotherapy while trying to handle school and football was “heavy in ways that are difficult to put into words.”

On one particularly rough day against Oregon State (Oct. 14, 2023), he completed just 42% of his passes, threw three interceptions, and was sacked five times—his internal state showing up on the field. He lost the starting job soon after and transferred.

His mother was declared cancer-free in the summer of 2024. Moore has spoken about how support from family, friends, and mental-health resources helped him, noting that as a young Black man reaching out for help often felt like “climbing an uphill battle.”

He has since advocated for greater mental-health access (including in a letter to Oregon’s governor) and continued supporting cancer awareness.

Around the same period, he also wrote a children’s book, From Journey to Dream (about a young boy nicknamed “Mr. 4000”), and has returned to Detroit to read it to kids at places like the Police Athletic League while donating to his high school, Martin Luther King.

He has described wanting kids from similar backgrounds to see that setbacks (including his own freshman-year struggles) are part of the journey.

text:
Two former Meta leaders started a data analytics company nearly six years ago.

On October 23, Meta bought it.

The company is Sundial. Co-founder Julie Zhuo was Meta's vice president of product design. Co-founder Chandra Narayanan was analytics chief at Sequoia Capital and Instagram, and earlier director of analytics at Facebook.

Sundial started before the AI wave and was rebuilt to be AI-native. The pitch was that anyone at a company could ask questions about its data in plain language and get reliable answers without filing a ticket with the data team. It combined AI, a company's own data context, and what it called expert playbooks. It also offered a workspace for writing SQL and Python and building dashboards.

Meta hasn't disclosed the price. Both founders are joining, along with other employees including Stanley Watt, Asa Levi, and John Maier. They go into a new Meta unit called Data Analytics Tooling & Agents, led by chief data officer Alex Schultz. Narayanan will run its analytics tooling and agents work. The unit handles descriptive analysis, runs experiments to test and improve data and AI products, and monitors critical AI systems with alerts.

Sundial had raised $23 million. A $16 million Series A in July 2025 was led by GPV's DJ Patil, with Sequoia, Electric Capital, Unusual Ventures, and Tribe Capital among the backers, along with angels including Fidji Simo, Tobi Lutke, and Drew Houston.

Instagram head Adam Mosseri called Zhuo and Narayanan two of the best people he has worked with.

text:
The Veridian Scepter is the central artifact of the original Oz adventure.

Dorothy, Glinda and Thorne's journey is organized around recovering its separated pieces. It offers a way to challenge the Wicked Witch and a way for Dorothy to get home. Its value brings those goals together, even though getting back to Kansas and deciding Oz's future are very different concerns.

An incomplete artifact creates practical limitations. Finding one piece doesn't finish the job. The group has to keep travelling, protect what it has found and survive the dangers around the remaining pieces. The last piece's location in the Emerald City makes the city part of the quest as well as a place threatened by the approaching enemy.

This entry stays with that first Oz series. Later Oz stories shouldn't be used to fill in powers or history that haven't been established at that point.

And although Dorothy's name makes the familiar slippers an obvious association, the artifact driving this particular adventure is the Scepter.

What are the new heaven and the new earth?
Answer
In Revelation 21:1, John sees something spectacular: “Then I saw ‘a new heaven and a new earth,’ for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away.” This new earth and new heaven are sometimes referred to as the “eternal state.” As seen in Revelation chapters 21—22, the new earth will be the eternal dwelling place of believers in Jesus Christ. Scripture gives us a few details of the new heaven and new earth.

The current heaven and earth have long been subject to God’s curse because of mankind’s sin. All creation “has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth” (Romans 8:22) as it awaits the fulfillment of God’s plan and “the children of God to be revealed” (verse 19). Heaven and earth will pass away (Mark 13:31), and they will be replaced by the new heaven and the new earth. At that time, the Lord, seated on His throne, says, “I am making everything new!” (Revelation 21:5). In the new creation, sin will be totally eradicated, and “there shall be no more curse” (Revelation 22:3, NKJV).

The new heaven and new earth are also mentioned in Isaiah 65:17; 66:22; and 2 Peter 3:13. Peter says that the new heaven and new earth will be “where righteousness dwells.” Isaiah says that “the former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.” Things will be completely new, and the old order of things, with the accompanying sorrow and tragedy, will be gone.

The new earth will be free from sin, evil, sickness, suffering, and death. It will be earth as God originally intended it to be, prior to the curse of sin. It will be Eden restored.

A major feature of the new earth will be the New Jerusalem. John calls it “the Holy City . . . coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband” (Revelation 21:2). This glorious city, with its streets of gold and pearly gates, is situated on a new, glorious earth. The tree of life will be there (Revelation 22:2). This city represents the final state of redeemed mankind, forever in fellowship with God: “God’s dwelling place is now among the people, and he will dwell with them. They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God. . . . His servants will serve him. They will see his face” (Revelation 21:3; 22:3–4).

In the new heaven and new earth, Scripture says, there are seven things notable for their absence—seven things that are “no more”:
• no more sea (Revelation 21:1)
• no more death (Revelation 21:4)
• no more mourning (Revelation 21:4)
• no more weeping (Revelation 21:4)
• no more pain (Revelation 21:4)
• no more curse (Revelation 22:3)
• no more night (Revelation 22:5)

The creation of the new heaven and new earth brings the promise that God “will wipe every tear from their eyes” (Revelation 21:4). This event comes after the tribulation, after the Lord’s second coming, after the millennial kingdom, after the final rebellion, after the final judgment of Satan, and after the great white throne judgment. The brief description of the new heaven and new earth is the last glimpse into eternity that the Bible gives.

I listened to your recent discussion with @Dr_Samkazibwe on The Observer Podcast regarding the Middle East and America’s game of hegemony. I wanted to offer a different, structurally grounded perspective on how these interlocking global pieces fit together.
My core argument is that we must discard the surface-level, legalistic narratives handed down by governments and examine the raw material, economic, and strategic chess pieces moving beneath them.

1. Venezuela: Drugs, Oil, and China
Consider Venezuela. On January 3, 2026, the United States executed Operation Absolute Resolve, a massive military operation that bombed Venezuelan infrastructure, killed dozens of security personnel, and forcefully captured President Nicolás Maduro to bring him to New York on narco-terrorism charges. While Washington framed this as an enforcement of international law and a strike against human rights abuses, the underlying architecture is pure energy geopolitics.
Venezuela holds the world's largest proven oil reserves. Before the invasion, Caracas had systematically leaned on Beijing as its vital economic lifeline, selling deeply discounted crude to China to bypass earlier U.S. sanctions. Immediately following the capture, the U.S.-backed interim administration of Delcy Rodríguez moved swiftly to reopen the Venezuelan oil sector to massive foreign corporate investment.
This was not just about local drug cartels; it was a targeted campaign to choke off China's long-term energy contracts in South America and violently strip a formidable adversary of a strategic foothold in America's immediate geographic backyard.

2. Iran: A Strategic Conflict Far Beyond the Middle East
When the United States and Israel escalated their military engagements with Iran, the public focus remained entirely on Tehran's nuclear program and regional proxy networks. However, the economic fallout points to a much larger target: China's supply chains.
Despite intense western economic warfare, Iran remained one of China's most resilient energy suppliers, funneling heavily discounted oil into Beijing’s independent domestic refineries. By disrupting these trade pipelines and forcing volatility into Middle Eastern oil infrastructure, the West effectively targeted China's primary energy cushion. The real collateral damage of the war in Iran is the disruption of Chinese manufacturing margins and its broader resource security in the Middle East.

3. Russia and Ukraine: The Universal Realism of Spheres of Influence
The world rightly condemned Moscow's brutal violation of Ukrainian sovereignty, pointing out Russia’s desperation to halt Kyiv's integration into NATO and the West. However, to understand the global structure, we must apply the security principle consistently.
The rationale Moscow uses to defend its security perimeter in Eastern Europe is functionally identical to the rationale Washington deployed to justify bombing Caracas. Just as the United States will not tolerate an economic or military alliance that allows an adversary like China to anchor itself in Latin America, Russia views Western military expansion on its immediate border as an existential threat. Great powers, by their very nature, refuse to be indifferent to the strategic alignments of neighboring states. The global analytical community cannot decry sphere-of-influence politics in Europe while remaining silent when the West actively enforces its own.

Excellent analysis by my friend Laura Ruggeri:

In Serbia the so-called "student-led" opposition won Sunday’s snap parliamentary election. Turnout approached 70%, the highest since the breakup of Yugoslavia, and presidential elections are now due by the end of December. 

The vote followed nearly two years of mass protests triggered by the November 2024 collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad, which killed 16 people. The tragedy was immediately weaponised as a symbol of corruption and official irresponsibility, a familiar technique of colour revolutions. The “Student List” borrowed the same methods used in Georgia and Ukraine: networked structures and a single anti-corruption agenda to broaden its appeal, while deliberately keeping disputes over Russia, NATO and Kosovo out of the campaign. The result was not an ordinary opposition party but a broad coalition of voters with very different views, united only by hostility to Vučić. 

Vučić's long, opaque rule and balancing act between Russia and the EU obviously created discontent in both the pro-Russian and the pro-EU camps. 

What's next? Even if the “Student List” has written into its programme both the absence of sanctions against Russia and continuity on Kosovo, Russia is losing a predictable negotiating partner. The new leadership is far less homogeneous, far more inexperienced and therefore more vulnerable to Western pressure. This does not mean Serbia will inevitably join sanctions but Russian influence can be reduced through revised energy contracts, changes in ownership structures and gradual alignment of legislation with EU rules. The West knows how to squeeze a small country. Keep in mind that the EU accounted for 58.3% of Serbian foreign trade, and in 2024 the Serbian government signed a controversial agreement with Brussels on lithium and battery technologies, which students opposed due to environmental concerns in the Jadar Valley, home to one of Europe's largest known lithium deposits.  

Brussels may offer Serbia a "development programme" (bribes) and EU prospects in exchange for two key conditions: imposing sanctions on Russia and recognising Kosovo. While no Serbian leader would recognise Kosovo, a "working compromise" for the EU could be the fulfillment of the first condition, sanctions on Russia.

Competition - People can offer different variants for same kind of service in tech and still co-exist. Look at how many SQL database offerings major clouds provide. They could converge all of them into one. But the different options are the feature here. Same will go with "AI first compute" or "AI assistants" or "AI serverless workflows" offered by Anthropic and others in the future. 
Supply - This is where things are interesting. At the end of the day, all of this requires hardware. And only a handful of companies are producing it. I think very soon we will see innovation and a new race here.

text:
Dear Saas founders,
Here are 8 prompts to craft posts that will convert 90% of the time

👇🏾

1. The "Warning Before You Launch" Hook (Same structure as original)
Write a Reddit post targeting indie hackers or solopreneurs who are about to launch a SaaS product. Open with a warning hook like "If you're about to launch your first SaaS… read this first." Establish credibility in 2–3 sentences (years of experience, relevant background). List 4–6 numbered, bolded mistakes people make before launching, each with a practical fix or prompt. 
Keep a conversational, non-preachy tone. End with a soft mention of a tool you built for yourself, offer to share it without pushing it, and close with a genuine question to the reader. Length: ~400–500 words.

2. The "I Did It Wrong So You Don't Have To" Confession Hook
Write a Reddit post where you share a painful mistake you made (e.g., lost $3k in AWS bills, got hacked, lost all your users overnight). Open with the outcome first: "I lost $3,000 in one night because of a single line of code." Then walk backwards through what happened. List the 3–5 root causes with bold headers. 
End with what you'd do differently and a question asking if others have had similar experiences. Tone: honest, slightly self-deprecating, but educational. Length: ~400 words.

3. The "Nobody Talks About This" Contrarian Hook
Write a Reddit post that challenges a common belief in a tech or startup community. Open with: "Everyone tells you to [popular advice]. Nobody tells you [the hidden downside]." List 4–5 counterintuitive truths with bold headers and short explanations. Use phrases like "this cost me 3 months" or "I see this constantly." End with a nuanced take that shows you're not just being contrarian — you actually care. Close with a question. Length: ~350–450 words.

4. The "Quick Sanity Check" Listicle Hook
Write a Reddit post framed as a checklist for a specific audience (e.g., people using no-code tools, first-time freelancers, new YouTubers). Open with: "Before you [take a major action], here's a quick sanity check." Use 5–7 numbered items with bold titles. Each item should have 2–3 bullet points of practical detail. Include one item that most people completely ignore. Mention a tool or resource you use personally. End with an open question. Length: ~450–500 words.

5. The "I Reviewed 100 [Things] So Here's What I Found" Data Hook
Write a Reddit post where you share patterns from a large sample you've personally observed (e.g., 100 portfolios, 50 landing pages, 30 cold emails). Open with the number upfront: "I've reviewed 100 indie hacker landing pages. Here's what almost all of them get wrong." List the top 4–5 patterns with bold headers. Be specific — name the exact mistake and the fix. Avoid being condescending; frame it as "easy to miss" not "stupid." Close with a soft CTA and a genuine question. Length: ~400 words.

6. The "This One Change Made a Big Difference" Transformation Hook
Write a Reddit post about a single specific change that had an outsized impact on your results (revenue, traffic, productivity, etc.). Open with the result: "One small change doubled my conversion rate." Spend the first third on context and credibility. Explain the change in detail with bold subsections. Acknowledge what didn't work before this. End with caveats (so it doesn't feel like a brag) and ask if others have found similar wins. Length: ~350–400 words.

7. The "Things I Wish Someone Told Me When I Started" Nostalgia Hook
Write a Reddit post addressed to your past self or to someone just starting out in a specific field (coding, freelancing, content creation, etc.). Open with: "I've been doing [X] for [Y] years. Here's what I wish someone told me on day one." List 5–6 lessons with bold titles. Mix practical tips with mindset shifts. Use personal anecdotes briefly (1–2 sentences each) to ground each point. End with humility — acknowledge you're still learning — and ask readers what they'd add. Length: ~450 words.

8. The "Free Tool / Resource Drop" Value Hook
Write a Reddit post where you share a free resource, tool, or system you built or use. Open by leading with the value: "I built a free [tool] that does [specific thing]. Here's how it works and why I made it." Explain the problem it solves first (2–3 sentences). Show how it works with a short walkthrough or bullet list. Preemptively address "why is this free?" or "what's the catch?" End with a genuine invitation for feedback and a question about what else people would find useful. Tone: generous, not salesy. Length: ~300–400 words.

We gave a founder 15 hours back last month.

He closed two deals in that time - deals he would've spent writing LinkedIn posts.

We've been running our done-for-you content system across 40+ founders for the past 8 months.

Every niche. SaaS, consulting, finance, health tech.

Different audiences. Different offers. The pattern is always the same.

Here's what we keep seeing:

→ Founders spend 15-20 hours a week writing, scheduling, engaging on content. That's a part-time job on top of running a company.

→ They get 12-30 likes per post. Months go by. Zero inbound leads.

→ Their competitors who have a team running content show up everywhere - LinkedIn, newsletters, podcasts - without touching a keyboard for creation.

→ Founders who hand this off get those hours back - and the results beat DIY every time.

This isn't "write better posts."

This is "stop doing $50/hour work when your time is worth $500/hour."

We pulled the numbers across our client base last quarter:

→ Average profile visits: 18/day to 280/day within 60 days

→ Average inbound leads: 0-2/week to 8-12/week

→ One SaaS founder signed a five-figure retainer from a single post we built. He didn't write a word.

→ Another went from 2,400 to 11,000 followers in 45 days. We mapped the strategy. We wrote every post. She approved it in 20 minutes.

And here's what most founders don't want to hear:

The ones still writing their own content in 2025 aren't being scrappy. They're burning their most valuable asset - time - on a task with a proven, faster path.

If you're still:

manually writing 3-4 posts a week and hoping something lands

spending Sunday afternoons batching content instead of with your family

guessing which hooks will work with no data behind the decision

checking analytics, tweaking profiles, engaging in comments - all before 9am

trying to create, distribute, AND run a business

...you're playing a game that founders with teams stopped playing months ago.

The founders who moved early are now:

landing 5-15 warm inbound leads every week

closing deals from content alone - zero cold outreach

spending their mornings on sales calls, not Google Docs

watching their authority grow while they focus on what actually makes money

Same way founders stopped doing their own bookkeeping when the math stopped working, content is now a function you hand to a team - not a task you squeeze into weekends.

If you want those hours back, we handle everything - strategy, writing, posting, engagement. You approve the direction in 30 minutes a week and close the deals that come in.

text:
WHAT LULA’S RE-ELECTION TELLS US: The Class War Need Not End in Fascism

On Sunday, Brazilians did something that the commentariat had told us was a lost cause. On the eve of his eighty-first birthday, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a former metalworker, turned the Trumpist, evangelical, neofascist, Zionist tide in Latin America to get re-elected President of Brazil. 

Three weeks earlier, he had come second in the first round, behind Flávio Bolsonaro, son and political heir of the man who trumpeted the merits of fascism, who had embraced Trump as his lord and master, who plotted a cynical coup against Brazilian democracy – moreover, the main candidates that were eliminated were rightists whose voters were meant to move to Bolsonaro. Yesterday, Lula overturned this deficit and won with a margin of nearly four and a half million votes.

I want to use Lula’s victory to tell a broader story. A story about a war, the class war that the few are waging against the many across the Western world. And a story about how that war need not end, as so many now fear, in a neofascist revival.

THE HIDDEN CLASS WAR

“There’s class warfare, all right,” Warren Buffett once said, “but it’s my class, the rich class, that’s making war, and we’re winning.” Mr Buffett was not exaggerating. For almost four decades, Western governments and central banks have pulled every policy lever in the same direction: to make the assets of the few burgeon at the expense of the incomes of the many.

Consider the numbers. Between 1952 and 1988, economic growth explained nearly all the gains of the West’s stock market. From 1989 onwards, growth explains only about a quarter. The largest share, around 40 per cent, came from income diverted from workers to shareholders. Another third came from cheaper money and lower perceived risk. That is not wealth creation. It is wealth extraction: a transfer from those who work to those who own, inflated by cheap money and paraded on the evening news as “a strong economy”.

Then look at the rescues. 2001, 2008, 2020, the British gilt crisis of 2022, Silicon Valley Bank in 2023: each time, the state rushed in to save the asset holders. Together they reveal the rule: to save the economy, you must save the wealth of those who own it – not those who produce stuff, not even productive companies. In the United States, the top tenth own almost 90 per cent of all shares. The Fed and the US federal government insure it for them, doing ‘whatever it takes’ to prop them up whenever their prices tank. The rest of us in the West pay the premium, in the form of the austerity that always follows the bailout.

And the owners need never sell. Why do billionaires pay so little tax? Because they do not earn incomes - they accumulate capital gains, taxed only when sold. So they borrow against their soaring assets at 1 or 2 per cent and live on the loan. Then they die and pay no tax on their capital gains, passing on the loot to their kids at ridiculously low inheritance taxes. Meanwhile, to pay bills and put food on the table, the worker borrows on a credit card at 20 per cent, her debts the mirror image of their fortunes.

Then, a large chunk of these accumulating assets seek even higher rents in places like Brazil where the US government intervenes to ensure that the local governments will also place the defence of these assets’ values above all else.

CAPITAL IS NOT A THING, NOT MERELY AN ASSET

Why does austerity keep returning, even though it is economically self-defeating? Marx tells the story of Thomas Peel, who in 1829 sailed to Western Australia’s Swan River with £50,000 of provisions and three hundred working-class men, women and children. On arrival, his workers walked off into the bush and worked for themselves. Peel had brought money, tools and labour, but he could not bring capitalism along, because his workers had an alternative.

Capital, Marx concluded, is not a thing but a social relation: the power of those who own to get those who don’t own to do things they’d rather did not do. Austerity is not an economic policy. It is a disciplinary device, keeping the many sufficiently insecure and indebted to accept whatever is on offer. The ruling class’s deepest fear is not inflation or debt. It is to end up like Peel: rich, but without the power to compel.

IS FASCISM INEVITABLE?

Here is the part of the story that keeps so many of us awake at night. When centre-left politicians, from Bill Clinton, Barack Obama and Tony Blair to Gerhard Schröder, Francois Hollande and Andy Burnham abandoned the language of class, a void opened up in the working-class heartlands of the West. Into that void stepped a venomous storyteller with a century of experience in filling such voids: the recalcitrant far right, the rebranded fascists. They offer left-behind workers a story of dignity, then redirect their fury away from the owner who shipped their factory abroad or sold their council house to some fund and towards the migrant next door. It does not end the class war. It merely divides one side – the workers – to rule over them. It camouflages it.

From the red suburbs of Paris to south Piraeus, from England’s red wall to Italy’s rust belt in Taranto, from the American rust belt to eastern Germany, the pattern seems relentless. And so, a fatalism has set in: the class war waged from above, we are told, must inevitably end in a neofascist, racist, misogynist revival.

Brazil has just refuted this fatalism. Brazil knows the monster intimately. It lived through four years of Jair Bolsonaro, with his nostalgia for the military dictatorship. On 8 January 2023, his followers stormed the Congress, the Supreme Court and the presidential palace. Brazil’s far right is not a fringe. Unlike Trump’s rag tag storm troopers, they had years of running a dictatorship. It won the first round of this election. They had the White House fully behind them, while the US Democrats, once again demonstrating their irrelevance, stayed mute. And yet, yesterday, they were defeated.

How? Not by hand-wringing about “populism”, nor by a centrist promise to manage the status quo more efficiently. Lula won because he did what the Western centre-left forgot how to do: he spoke the language of class, and backed it with policies that shifted power, however modestly, from the few to the many. His government exempted those earning up to five thousand reals a month from income tax and paid for it with a minimum tax on the very richest. During Brazil’s G20 presidency, it proposed a global minimum tax on billionaires. When Lula tells Brazilian workers that the elites have rigged the game, he points his finger upwards, at the rentier and the speculator, not sideways, at the migrant or the poor.

PIX – AN EXAMPLE OF AN ANTI-OLIGARCHY DIGITAL TOOL

But the most innovative weapon in Brazil’s arsenal is one that few outside Latin America have heard of. It is called Pix.

Every time you tap a card to pay for a coffee, a toll is levied. Visa, Mastercard and the banks take a cut, often 2 or 3 per cent, from every transaction. Multiply this by billions of purchases a day and you grasp one of the most lucrative rent-extraction machines ever devised. These are not profits made in competitive markets but rent extracted by those who own the digital rails on which our economic lives now run. It is part of what I call technofeudalism.

Unlike Britain, Europe or, of course, America, Brazil’s central bank moved to limit this rabid exploitation. It launched an alternative: a public, instant payment system, free for individuals and with capped fees for merchants. A Brazilian pays a street vendor in Salvador or sends money to her mother in Recife, instantly, using Pix from her phone, with no card company or bank taking its slice. Brazilians took to it with astonishing enthusiasm. Last year, Pix processed almost 80 billion transactions and overtook credit cards as the most popular way to pay online.

Pix is, in effect, the Swan River of the digital age. It gave tens of millions of Brazilians, including the poorest, who had never had a bank card, an alternative to the toll booths of Big Finance. And, like Peel, the toll collectors did not take it lying down. This summer, Washington imposed 25 per cent tariffs on most Brazilian exports, and its trade representative explicitly named Pix as a grievance, complaining that it “unfairly disadvantaged” American payment companies! The most powerful government on Earth deployed its trade arsenal against a free public service for being too successful at denying rents to Visa and Mastercard.

Lula did not blink. He defended Pix as a Brazilian public good, and Brazilians rewarded him for it. Here, at last, is a concrete example of limiting the power of Big Business, Big Finance and Big Tech: not with slogans, but by building public digital infrastructure that removes the opportunity to extract rent in the first place.

NOT A REVOLUTION, BUT AN AUSPICIOUS PORTENT

Let me not romanticise. Lula is no revolutionary. His margin was narrow. Brazil’s Congress remains in the grip of agribusiness and evangelical blocs. Its central bank still keeps interest rates punishingly high, a weapon of the class war if ever there was one. Lula himself has compromised much too much with these vested interests, and lost support as a result.

But Brazil has shown three things the rest of us must learn. First, the class war waged against the many does not have to end in fascism. Fascism wins only when the left vacates the battlefield of class. Second, a progressive government can win by pointing upwards, at those who extract rent, rather than downwards, at those who suffer. And third, Big Business can be defeated, at least forced to lose some battles, by building public alternatives to its rent-extracting machines.

So, here is the challenge to Britain, to Europe, to the people of the United States. 

-Build your own Pix: public payment rails that end the tolls of Visa and Mastercard. 
-Tax capital gains, ill-gotten wealth that is, not just income. 
-Make every rescue conditional, with the public receiving real, permanent equity in return. 
-Create a public investment bank as an alternative to the bond markets. Restore the bargaining power of the workforce. And give working people what Peel’s workers found at Swan River: an alternative, and the freedom to say no.

Buffett was right. There is a class war, and his class has been winning hands down. But yesterday, in Brazil, it lost a battle though not the war. It lost because a working-class president dared to name the war and fight it using weapons fashioned to defend the many.

Tata Motors India will acquire Italian Iveco Group for $4.4 billion after shareholders accepted the tender offer at a decisive 87.81% rate, locking in control of the European truck making giant.

This deal instantly elevates Tata into the global top tier of commercial vehicle makers, fusing Indian scale with Iveco’s advanced truck, bus, and alternative-fuel technologies.

Tata already owns Jaguar Land Rover, which it acquired from Ford in 2008 for $2.3 billion and successfully rescued, turning the British icons into profitable global luxury brands.

India is winning in electric mobility: over 2,500,000 EVs registered so far in 2026, up more than 50% year-on-year across two-wheelers, cars, and commercial vehicles.

Tata Motors commands roughly 40% of India’s electric car market, leading the charge in clean transportation with models that are winning both volume and share.

India’s auto components industry has surged to $86 billion in annual turnover, with exports hitting a record $24 billion and more than doubling over the past decade.

Indian component makers now supply precision parts to Europe, North America, and beyond, cementing the country as a critical node in global automotive supply chains.

The Iveco acquisition adds electric buses, advanced powertrains, and connectivity tech, accelerating Tata’s ability to compete head-to-head with the world’s biggest truck makers.

Combined, Tata and Iveco create a commercial vehicle powerhouse with roughly $22 billion in revenue and a presence spanning India, Europe, and the Americas.

From rescuing Jaguar Land Rover to buying Iveco, Indian companies are no longer just participants, they are rewriting the rules of global industry.

Backed by the world’s fastest-growing major economy and a booming EV and components ecosystem, India is exporting engineering excellence, not just products.

The message is unmistakable: the future of global mobility is being built by India, and the world depends on India to keep moving.

text:
🇨🇳 CHINA’S AI STOCK BOOM HAS TAKEN A BRUTAL TURN, COULD THE U.S. BE NEXT?

China’s tech sell-off is raising a bigger question for global markets: what happens when investors stop paying premium prices for the AI story?

The chart tells part of the story.

📉 China’s STAR 50 Science and Technology Innovation Index has fallen 12.79% over six months, dropping from its July peak of around 2,186 to approximately 1,316.

But the bigger concern is the concentration of money in AI.

Here’s why investors are paying attention:

• Valuations ran hot: Some Chinese AI stocks traded at extremely high earnings multiples, leaving little room for disappointment.

• The sell-off spread: AI models, semiconductor suppliers and robotics companies all came under pressure as enthusiasm cooled.

• Retail speculation amplified the boom: Heavy trading and crowded positions can make reversals more painful when sentiment changes.

Now look at the US market.

AI remains one of Wall Street’s biggest investment themes, with a handful of mega-cap technology companies accounting for a substantial share of index performance.

The concern isn’t that AI is a bad investment. It’s that even a transformative technology can become dangerously overpriced.

If earnings fail to justify expectations, investors may start repricing companies across the entire AI ecosystem.

China’s correction doesn’t prove that the US is heading for the same outcome. But it offers a useful reminder: strong technology trends and rising stock prices are not the same thing.

The concern is no longer just how big AI will become. It’s how much future growth investors have already priced in.

"Although few details of the ACF have so far been disclosed, Trappier says it “will be smaller than we expected with the NGF”.

"Power will likely come from a further evolution of the Safran Aircraft Engines M88, beyond the T-Rex variant currently in development for the F5-standard Rafale."

If this means France is giving up on creating a next-gen engine core, that's truly disappointing news. I guess the financial struggle is real given their other issues.

Right now it appears they're basically aiming for a Rafale-sized jet but with internal weapon bays, evolutionary advancements in tech & an upgraded M88++ core for the powerplant. This will certainly be less expensive to develop compared to a larger air superiority-focused jet with a 6th gen engine, but there will also be a SIGNIFICANT capability penalty when compared with likes of GCAP, F-47 or Chinese J-XDS especially in the A2A department and also in EW potential.

This may suit France's projected needs sufficiently given Russia's own struggles, but I don't see this being well suited for IAF's potential future requirements.

text:
Today in History 
October 27th
1880
Theodore Roosevelt Marries Alice Hathaway Lee on His 22nd Birthday

On October 27, 1880, Theodore Roosevelt, the future 26th president of the United States, married Alice Hathaway Lee in Brookline, Massachusetts. The birthday wedding began a love story that ended tragically less than four years later.

Roosevelt met Alice in October 1878 while attending Harvard University. Born on July 29, 1861, she was the daughter of prominent Boston banker George Cabot Lee and Caroline Haskell Lee. Her charm, intelligence, and lively personality captivated the young Roosevelt, who affectionately called her “Sunshine.” He pursued her enthusiastically, though she was initially hesitant to return his feelings.

Their courtship blossomed, and on Valentine’s Day, February 14, 1880, they became engaged. Roosevelt was 21, and Alice was 18. His diaries reveal his devotion. They married that autumn at the First Parish Church in Brookline, surrounded by family and friends.

Roosevelt had graduated from Harvard earlier in 1880 and was beginning to decide how to use his considerable energy and ambition. After the wedding, he studied law at Columbia University but soon turned toward public service. The couple traveled in Europe in 1881, when Roosevelt climbed the Matterhorn, showing his adventurous spirit.

In November 1881, Roosevelt won election to the New York State Assembly at age 23. Alice shared the excitement of his early political career, while the couple looked forward to establishing a family home. In 1883, as Alice was expecting their first child, Roosevelt began planning a house in Oyster Bay, Long Island. He initially called the project Leeholm in her honor; it later became known as Sagamore Hill.

On February 12, 1884, Alice gave birth to a daughter, also named Alice. Roosevelt was in Albany attending to legislative business when news arrived that his wife was gravely ill. He hurried to New York, where two crises unfolded in the family home. On February 14, his mother, Martha Bulloch Roosevelt, died of typhoid fever. Hours later, Alice died from Bright’s disease, a kidney disorder, at just 22 years old.

The date was especially cruel: February 14 was the fourth anniversary of the couple’s engagement. Stricken with grief, Roosevelt marked his diary with a large black X and wrote, “The light has gone out of my life.” He later composed a private tribute to Alice, but rarely spoke publicly about her.

Roosevelt sought distance from his sorrow in the Dakota Territory, spending long periods ranching, riding, and hunting. His daughter was cared for primarily by his sister Anna during this period. The frontier experience helped shape his conservation outlook.

In December 1886, Roosevelt married his childhood friend Edith Kermit Carow. He returned to politics and eventually became president in September 1901 after William McKinley’s assassination. Yet the happiness and loss of his first marriage remained an important part of his personal story.

The wedding on Roosevelt’s 22nd birthday offers a glimpse of the man behind the larger-than-life statesman: a young husband filled with hope, whose sudden bereavement profoundly altered the course of his life. #OTD

text:
Behind every Ugandan business that is struggling today because of the high dollar rate is someone who took a risk, borrowed money, invested their savings, and dared to dream of a better future.

But when the dollar rate rises, the pain goes far beyond the exchange bureaus. And sadly our government, parliament or those in authority don’t seem to offer any possible solution. 

A business owner who imports goods has to spend more money to bring in the same products. The cost of machinery, spare parts, raw materials, fuel and other essential supplies goes up. Rent, salaries and other operating expenses still have to be paid. Yet customers are also struggling, and increasing prices is becoming harder because people simply cannot afford as much as they used to.

So the business owner is trapped. Increase prices and risk losing customers. Keep prices the same and watch your profits disappear.

Some businesses are surviving on borrowed money. Others are cutting jobs, reducing stock, postponing expansion or quietly closing their doors. And behind every struggling business are workers with families to feed, children to educate and bills that cannot wait.

What hurts most is that many of these entrepreneurs are not lazy, careless or incapable. They are people who wake up every morning determined to make something work, but the economic pressure keeps getting heavier.

And let us remember something: when a business closes, it is not just the owner who suffers. Employees lose jobs. Suppliers lose customers. Landlords lose tenants. Families lose income. The entire economy feels the impact.

Yes, a stronger dollar can benefit some exporters and Ugandans receiving money from abroad. But for businesses that depend heavily on imported goods and materials, a rising dollar can be devastating, especially when they cannot pass the extra costs on to their customers.

My question is, how do we expect Ugandan businesses to grow, employ more people and contribute to the economy when the cost of doing business keeps rising?

We need a business environment where entrepreneurs can plan, invest, employ and grow without constantly fearing that exchange rate movements will wipe out their hard earned progress.

text:
The place I was born in killed my dreams before I even had the chance to dream them. The future died here long before I was old enough to understand what a future was supposed to look like.

My entire life has revolved around hoping for the bare minimum. The most basic necessities of life are privileges here. This isn’t living. It’s surviving, day after day, in a country that has been exhausted for decades, where you’re always afraid, always waiting for something terrible to happen, and slowly losing your passion for everything around you. You go to sleep never knowing if you’ll wake up the next morning, or if you’ll wake up to the news that someone you love is gone. We’ve been denied the most basic human rights for as long as we can remember. We’ve spent our entire lives being afraid.

The only thing that ever gave me a glimpse of another life was traveling. But even that was never something I could simply decide to do. Visas cost a fortune, and no matter how much you prepare, how much you save, or how badly you want to see the world, everything can come crashing down in a second because of the passport you were born with. A passport that feels like a punishment for a nationality I never chose.

So I learned to live somewhere else in my head.

My body stayed here, but my mind, my dreams, and the person I truly was existed somewhere far away from the reality I was forced to live in. I built an entire utopia inside my head and lived there because the real world had so little to offer me. I became a person who was physically present in one place but emotionally and mentally living in another, because being fully present in my own reality was sometimes more than I could bear.

And then I found BTS.

They helped me cope with a life that has given me so many reasons to feel hopeless. They gave me something to look forward to, something to be excited about, something that made the days feel a little less unbearable. And even with all the rumors, the mistakes, the arguments, and the endless drama within this fandom, I need people to understand something: the reality I live in is so much harder than any of that. So much uglier than any fanwar or controversy could ever be. I’m not saying this to invalidate anyone else’s struggles. I’m saying it because I genuinely hope none of you ever have to experience what it’s like to grow up in a place that slowly takes away your sense of possibility, your security, and your belief that life could ever be different.

And God, this year has been so hard.

Every year here is hard, but this one has been among the hardest for a reason that is difficult to explain to anyone who hasn’t lived through something similar. We were told, in name at least, that we had been liberated from war. But the truth is that you don’t simply leave a war behind because someone declares it over. Some of us will spend the rest of our lives growing up inside it, carrying its consequences, its fear, and its devastation long after the world decides it’s time to move on.

And perhaps the cruelest part is that, for a little while, I genuinely believed things could finally get better. I thought maybe we could catch up with the rest of the world, maybe we could finally participate in it instead of watching from the sidelines, maybe we could stop feeling like outsiders in a world we were born into just like everyone else.

At the beginning of this year, I found hope in the most unexpected way. I managed to get BTS concert tickets. I actually managed to make it happen. I was going to travel to a beautiful country, see a beautiful place, and, for once, experience something that wasn’t defined by everything I had been deprived of.

And suddenly, I had something to live toward +

text:
Betelguese... Betelguese... Betelguese 👻 🕷️

Betelguese’s Great Dimming in late 2019 and early 2020 was linked to an episode in which expelled material cooled and formed dust, obscuring part of the star. 

Observations taken before the dimming had already revealed unusually cool gas and changes in the structure of its extended atmosphere, consistent with a shock wave passing through the outer layers.

New research follows what happened afterward, using the Very Large Array and ALMA. Observations collected between 2021 and 2026 cover seven frequencies, from 22 to 485 GHz. 

Different radio wavelengths reveal gas at different distances from the visible surface, allowing the team to examine both the temperature profile and the changing shape of the atmosphere.

The measurements show that the outer atmosphere has warmed since the unusually low temperatures recorded in 2019. The researchers found a brightness temperature, a temperature inferred from the radio emission, of around 3,500 K at approximately 2.7 stellar radii from the centre, falling to about 2,220 K closer in, at 1.2 stellar radii. This confirms a cool region between the visible surface and the hotter chromosphere, overlapping the molecular layer known as the MOLsphere. The radio measurements also indicate that relatively cool material remains mixed with hotter gas, which ultraviolet observations preferentially detect.

Another part of the investigation concerns Siwarha, Betelgeuse’s recently identified companion. Its roughly six-year orbit lies within the supergiant’s extended atmosphere, about 2.3 stellar radii from the centre. This orbital period offers an explanation for Betelgeuse’s long brightness cycle, alongside its shorter pulsation cycle of approximately 400 days. Earlier optical and ultraviolet spectroscopy had revealed changes in gas absorption and outflow that followed the expected orbital cycle. Those results support a model in which the companion’s gravity concentrates gas into a trailing, expanding wake as it moves through the atmosphere.

The new radio data add spatial evidence. Betelgeuse’s radio-emitting atmosphere appears slightly more elongated when Siwarha is expected to reach its greatest apparent separation, and rounder when the companion passes in front of or behind the supergiant. Siwarha itself is too faint to detect in these radio observations; the evidence comes from the changing shape of the surrounding gas.

These correlations are consistent with periodic atmospheric disturbances caused by the companion, although more observations across its orbit are needed to test the interpretation. 

The study provides a way to investigate how a nearby companion interacts with the extended atmosphere of a massive, evolved star.

Unit 3: Phase 1 is operational, supporting the next phase of growth.
Testing Facilities: In-house EMC, navigation and calibration facilities are being installed to reduce production delays caused by external testing.
Defence Pipeline: The company is pursuing opportunities across Pinaka, QRSAM, heavyweight torpedoes, Varunastra and Pralay programmes.
Premier Explosives: CCI approval has been received, and the acquisition process is progressing towards the open offer.
Shauryastra Defence Systems: Apollo holds a 34% stake in the associate company, which will focus on developing complete weapon systems and longer-range platforms.

3. Order Book & Major Orders
Current Order Book: Approximately ₹1,765 Cr as of September 30, 2026.
MIGM: The Indian Navy order is expected by February 2027. If secured, it could increase the order book to ₹4,500–5,000 Cr.
Pinaka: RFQ submitted for 300 units under the MIL case, with orders expected before December-end.
Heavyweight Torpedo: A 30-unit order through BDL is expected to be finalised in November, with delivery within nine months.
Varunastra: Management expects an order worth ₹100 Cr or more.
QRSAM & Pralay: Apollo is pursuing opportunities in missile systems and complete weapon manufacturing.

4. Management Guidance
FY27 Revenue Growth: 35–45% YoY on a standalone basis.
H2 Execution: Management is targeting 35–45% higher execution in H2 compared with H1.
MIGM Order: Expected by February 2027, with the timeline not extending beyond March FY27, according to management.
Order Book: ₹4,500–5,000 Cr by March 2027, subject to MIGM order placement.
Unit 3: Full operational readiness targeted by March 2027.
Operating Cash Flow: Annual positive operating cash flow expected from FY29 onwards.
Long-Term Vision: An aspirational group-level revenue target of ₹25,000 Cr over five years.

5. Capex & Capacity Expansion
Unit 3 Expansion: Once fully operational, the facility is expected to provide nearly 12 times the capacity of the existing facility.
Timeline: Full operational readiness targeted by March 2027.
Testing Infrastructure: In-house EMC, navigation and calibration facilities are expected to become operational within one month.
IDL Expansion: Management discussed plans for 15 types of manufacturing plants and the acquisition of an additional 2,000 acres near Hyderabad, alongside 1,200 acres already held. Specific capex figures and a detailed turnaround plan were not disclosed.

6. Margins & Cash Flow
Standalone EBITDA margin reached 35%, supported by a higher contribution from production orders.
Management cautioned that margins may fluctuate depending on the mix of production and development projects.
The standalone tax rate was approximately 51% in Q2, affecting PAT conversion.
H1 FY27 operating cash flow was positive at ₹22 Cr.
Working capital stood at 353 days, improving from 359 days in FY26.

7. Key Things to Track
Actual placement and timing of the MIGM order.
Execution required to achieve FY27 revenue guidance.
Order book movement towards ₹4,500–5,000 Cr.
Completion of the Premier Explosives acquisition.
Improvement in IDL's performance.
Sustainability of elevated EBITDA margins.
